fibreIdentityRule:
One named fibre presentation per actual native P cell: edge5-fibre:

. Retain the owning cell and all four actual face occurrences.
oppositePresentationRule: Associate that fibre with the E cell obtained by reflection through the selected reading's middle plane; transport all four face occurrences by the same geometric map. This is a declared presentation convention, not a physical path or derived endpoint transport law.
externalBoundaryRule: Both the chosen entry N body and its reflected exit N body expose the same eighty fibre identities as a retained bundle. Bundle occurrences are logical, body-attached occurrences; they are not eighty invented geometric faces.
boundaryPortDomainRule: Retain all four actual entry-forward shared faces and all four exit-backward shared faces as possible passage interfaces. Do not assign a fibre to one of them by lexical order or count.
portMultiplicityRule: Each P/E presentation has four coordinate-face occurrences. The 320 occurrences on each side do not create 320 independent fibre identities or payloads.
placementScope: Proposed first extension: one globally selected same-role-pair readout triple on the physical middle N plane, not an independent copy on each of the forty-four cones.
placementDomainRule: Enumerate every middle-plane transverse tip T and every ordered pair of distinct middle N neighbours U,V sharing a native edge with T. Tag U as the P/P site and V as the E/E site. Keep all candidates.
placementActivationObligation: A later complete routing must make both members of T's opposite-tip group active, supply the selected records at T,U,V, and specify the remaining cross-pair sites. Geometric triple eligibility does not prove those conditions.
referenceDomainRule: Retain the actual four entry-side reference cells and four joint N pairings under binding [0,0], without identifying their directional labels with fibre face axes.
notSupplied: paths between external bundle and body-wide fibre presentations
noClaims: all forty-four cones have independent copies of this triple
